title: Perfect maps into principal support are power torsion
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], let f be a global function on X, and let T=V(f). If alpha:E \to E' is a morphism in D_QCoh(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], E is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], and every cohomology sheaf of E' vanishes on X\setminus T, then f^n alpha=0 for some integer n\ge 0.

proof.text: Fix f,E,E\prime satisfying the hypotheses. For every open U define P(U) to mean: for all integers k and all local morphisms beta:R_U E -> R_U(E\prime[k]), some power of f times the source identity kills beta by precomposition. The affine case is [lem-sc-perfect-support-affine-open-torsion]. It is essential to quantify over arbitrary local morphisms and all shifts, since the Mayer--Vietoris lift need not be the restriction of a global map.

For a union U union V, take local annihilating exponents a,b for the two restrictions of beta. Restricted scalar identities multiply according to f^(a+b)=f^a f^b; naturality of the canonical derived restriction comparison moves precomposition through restriction. Thus f^(a+b) beta has both restrictions zero. Apply [lem-sc-derived-open-hom-scalar-mayer-vietoris] to lift it to gamma on U intersect V with target shifted by k-1. P(U intersect V) supplies c killing gamma. Scalar equivariance of the additive boundary gives f^(c+a+b) beta=delta(0)=0. The Lean proof carries out all these equalities, including choosing the order of a,b that kills each restriction.

Apply [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology-induction] to P and specialize to the top open. At the top, restriction of module sheaves is an equivalence: Modules.overFunctorEquiv identifies it with restriction along X.topIso.hom, whose inverse is restriction along X.topIso.inv; restrictFunctorComp, restrictFunctorCongr and restrictFunctorId give the two inverse isomorphisms. Its exact derived functor is therefore faithful. Apply P(top) in shift zero to the restriction of alpha followed by the inverse zero-shift isomorphism. Faithfulness reflects zero; cancel the zero-shift isomorphism, and identify precomposition by f^n times identity with schemeDerivedScalar X (f^n) alpha.hom. All these comparisons are proved in Lean in this module.
